en: to be old; to be long-established

examples.en: It is an old house.
This building is very old.
This computer is old. It's too slow.

explain: '오래되다'는 건물, 카페, 책, 휴대폰처럼 사물이 생긴 지 오래됐을 때 써요(오래된 건물, 오래된 책). 사람의 나이에는 쓰지 않아요. 사람은 '나이가 많다'나 '늙다'를 써요.

phrases.en: An old book smells nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 ‘오래된’으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes 오래된.

phrases.en: This shop is not old.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되지 않았다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say something is not old.

phrases.en: The house is old, so it's a bit cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 ‘-아/어서’로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connect with -아/어서 to give a reason.

dict_examples.ko: 쓰던 가전제품이 오래되고 낡아서 새것으로 바꿨다.
dict_examples.en: The appliance I'd been using was old and worn, so I replaced it with a new one.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: '오래되다' is for things that have been around a long time: a building, a café, a book, a phone (오래된 건물 an old building, 오래된 책 an old book). Don't use it for a person's age. For people, say 나이가 많다 or 늙다.

examples.en: My younger brother enters high school this year.

examples.ko: 고교 시절 친구들을 아직도 자주 만나요.
examples.en: I still often meet my friends from high school.

examples.ko: 이 지역 고교 중에서 우리 학교가 제일 커요.
examples.en: Among the high schools in this area, our school is the biggest.

examples.ko: 주말에 고교 야구 경기를 보러 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to see a high school baseball game on the weekend.
My uncle got a job right after finishing high school.
I heard a high school reunion is held next month.

explain: '고등학교'를 줄여 쓴 형태로, 뉴스 제목과 야구 대회 이름에서 많이 보여요. 말할 때는 '고등학교'를 그대로 쓰는 편이 많고, 학년은 '고3'처럼 '고'만 써요. '고교 시절', '고교 동창'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: I go to a high school in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 줄인 '고교'보다 '고등학교'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, the full 'godeung-hakgyo' is used more than 'gogyo'.

phrases.en: My high-schooler sibling studies late every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고교' 뒤에 '생'을 붙여 고등학생을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'saeng' after 'gogyo' means a high school student.

phrases.en: Yesterday I met a high school classmate after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 고등학교를 졸업한 친구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friend who graduated from the same high school.

explain_en: A shortened form of '고등학교', common in news headlines and baseball tournament names. In speech people often say the full '고등학교', and grade years use just '고' as in '고3'. It often attaches before other words, such as '고교 시절' or '고교 동창'.

t90.ax: I still often meet my friends from high school.

examples.en: I design bags at my company.

examples.ko: 건축가 친구가 우리 집을 직접 디자인했어요.
examples.en: My architect friend designed our house himself.

examples.ko: 우리 가게 로고를 직접 디자인하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to design our shop's logo myself.
How shall we design the poster for this event?

examples.ko: 디자인하는 일은 재미있지만 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Designing is fun, but it takes a long time.

examples.ko: 앱을 디자인하려면 쓰는 사람의 생각을 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To design an app, you need to know what its users think.

explain: 모양과 구성을 정하는 일이고, 실제로 만드는 것은 '만들다'를 써요. 그래서 '옷을 디자인해서 직접 만들었어요'처럼 두 동사를 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요. 직업은 '디자이너', 결과물은 '디자인'이라고 하고, '디자인이 예뻐요'처럼 명사로 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: I designed the bag and made it myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 정하는 일과 실제로 만드는 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the planning of the shape with the actual making.

phrases.en: I designed this poster myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 아니라 내가 했다는 점을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes that you did it yourself, not someone else.

phrases.example: 우리 가게 간판을 예쁘게 디자인해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please design our shop sign nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 디자인을 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone else to do a design for you.

explain_en: It means deciding the look and layout; actually making the thing is '만들다', so the two verbs often appear together: '옷을 디자인해서 직접 만들었어요'. The person is a '디자이너' and the result is '디자인'. In daily talk the noun is more common, as in '디자인이 예뻐요'.

t90.ax: I design bags at my company.

examples.en: I borrowed a history book from the library on the weekend.

examples.ko: 저는 한국 역사책을 읽고 나서 경복궁에 갔어요.
examples.en: After reading a Korean history book, I went to Gyeongbokgung.

examples.ko: 역사책 한 권을 일주일 만에 다 읽었어요.
examples.en: I finished a whole history book in one week.
My father's bookshelf has lots of history books.

examples.ko: 이 역사책은 그림이 많아서 어린이도 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This history book has many pictures, so even children can read it.

explain: '책' 앞에 분야를 붙이면 책 종류가 돼요. '역사책, 요리책, 만화책, 소설책'처럼요. 학교 수업용 책은 '교과서', 시험 공부를 돕는 책은 '참고서'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a history book at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책은 '권'으로 세어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Books are counted with 권.

phrases.en: Please recommend an interesting history book.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재미있는'처럼 꾸미는 말을 앞에 붙여 책을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a describing word like 재미있는 before it to describe the book.

phrases.en: Please bring your history textbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 수업에서 쓰는 역사책은 '역사 교과서'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A history book used in school classes is called 역사 교과서.

explain_en: Put a field before 책 to name a type of book: 역사책, 요리책, 만화책, 소설책. A school class book is a 교과서, and a study aid for exams is a 참고서.

examples.en: I received my diploma at school today.
If you lose your diploma, it's hard to get another.

examples.ko: 졸업장 위에 학교 이름과 제 이름이 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The school's name and my name are written on the diploma.

examples.ko: 대학교 졸업장을 받으려면 학점을 다 채워야 해요.
examples.en: To get a university diploma, you have to complete all your credits.
Please send the diploma and the transcript together.

explain: 졸업을 축하하는 행사는 '졸업식'이고, 거기서 받는 증서가 '졸업장'이에요. 나중에 서류로 필요할 때는 '졸업증명서'를 따로 뽑아요. '졸업장을 받다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The teacher gave diplomas to the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'의 반대로 주는 사람의 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 'receive', said from the giver's side.

phrases.en: I have to submit a graduation certificate to the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸업장은 증서이고, 졸업증명서는 서류로 따로 뽑아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The diploma is the certificate itself; the graduation certificate is a document you request separately.

phrases.example: 이 일은 졸업장이 있어야 지원할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You need a diploma to apply for this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for stating a requirement.

explain_en: The celebration is the 졸업식 and the certificate you receive there is the 졸업장. When you need proof later as a document, you get a separate 졸업증명서. Say '졸업장을 받다'.

examples.ko: 통역사가 외국 손님의 말을 한국어로 전해 줬어요.
examples.en: The interpreter passed the foreign guest's words on in Korean.
I want to become an interpreter someday.

examples.ko: 회의에는 통역사 두 명이 함께 참석했어요.
examples.en: Two interpreters attended the meeting together.

examples.ko: 통역사가 도와줘서 병원에서 설명을 잘 이해했어요.
examples.en: The interpreter helped me, so I understood the explanation at the hospital well.

examples.ko: 통역사는 두 언어를 아주 잘해야 해요.
examples.en: An interpreter has to be very good at two languages.

examples.ko: 그 통역사를 소개해 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you introduce me to that interpreter?

explain: 말을 바로 옮기는 사람은 '통역사', 글을 옮기는 사람은 '번역가'예요. 일은 '통역하다', '번역하다'로 구분해요. 직업 이름 끝에 '-사'가 붙는 말이 많아요(간호사, 요리사).

phrases.en: My friend interpreted for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통역사의 일을 동사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form for what an interpreter does.

phrases.en: We are looking for an interpreter for the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일할 사람을 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking for someone to work.

phrases.example: 통역사는 말을 옮기고 번역가는 글을 옮겨요.
phrases.en: An interpreter carries over speech, and a translator carries over writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통역사는 말, 번역가는 글을 옮기는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An interpreter handles speech; a translator handles writing.

explain_en: Someone who converts speech on the spot is a 통역사, and someone who converts writing is a 번역가. The jobs are 통역하다 and 번역하다. Many job names end in -사 (간호사, 요리사).

examples.ko: 첫돌 때 받은 금반지를 지금도 서랍에 보관하고 있어요.
examples.en: I still keep the gold ring I received on my first birthday in a drawer.
The price of a gold ring changes depending on the price of gold.
The gold ring is too small and won't go on my finger.

examples.ko: 결혼 선물로 금반지 한 쌍을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pair of gold rings as a wedding gift.
I asked them to engrave a name on the gold ring.

explain: 금으로 만든 반지예요. 한국에서는 아기의 첫돌에 선물하는 금반지를 '돌반지'라고 따로 불러요. 짝말로 '은반지'가 있고, 동사는 '끼다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Grandmother went to the market wearing a gold ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반지를 손가락에 착용할 때는 동사 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb 끼다 is used for wearing a ring on a finger.

phrases.en: Silver rings are cheaper than gold rings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금 대신 은으로 만든 반지로, 금반지의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A ring made of silver instead of gold; the counterpart to 금반지.

phrases.en: I gave my nephew a gold ring for his first birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기의 첫돌에 선물하는 금반지만 따로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A special name for the gold ring given for a baby's first birthday.

explain_en: It is a ring made of gold. In Korea, the gold ring given as a gift on a baby's first birthday has its own name, '돌반지'. Its counterpart is '은반지' (silver ring), and the verb is '끼다' (to wear).

examples.en: The back of my hair was flattened, so I wore a hat.
Check the shape of the back of your hair in the mirror.
At the salon I only had the back of my hair trimmed a little.
Someone stuck gum in the back of my hair.

explain: 머리 뒤쪽의 머리카락이에요. 머리 뒷부분 자체는 '뒤통수'예요. 짝이 되는 '앞머리'는 보통 이마를 덮는 짧은 머리를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: I tied my back hair into one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 모양을 말할 때 '묶다'와 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 묶다 (to tie) when talking about hairstyles.

phrases.en: I got the back of my hair cut short at the hair salon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미용실 이야기에서 '자르다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 자르다 (to cut) when talking about the hair salon.

phrases.en: The front hair is short and the back hair is long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말 '앞머리'와 같이 쓰면 머리 모양을 비교할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair it with its counterpart 앞머리 to compare parts of a hairstyle.

explain_en: This is the hair at the back of the head. The back of the head itself is '뒤통수'. The counterpart '앞머리' usually means the short hair over the forehead, like bangs.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 가슴에 작은 하트 마크가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: This shirt has a small heart mark on the chest.
I always check the recycling mark on the packaging.

examples.ko: 앱 아이콘에 빨간 마크가 생기면 새 알림이 온 거예요.
examples.en: When a red mark appears on the app icon, a new notification has come.

explain: 작은 그림이나 표시에 써요. '하트 마크', '별 마크', '재활용 마크'처럼 앞에 모양이나 이름이 붙어요. 회사의 상징은 '로고'도 많이 써요. 축구에서 상대 선수를 막는 '마크하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: There is a heart mark next to the message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양 이름 뒤에 '마크'를 붙여서 작은 그림을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 마크 after a shape name to refer to a small symbol.

phrases.en: The bottle has a recycling mark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건에 붙은 약속된 표시를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for standard symbols printed on products.

phrases.en: I put a check mark on the correct answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞는 답이나 끝낸 일에 표시하는 ✓ 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ✓ shape used to mark a correct answer or a finished task.

explain_en: It is used for small pictures or signs, with a shape or name in front, as in 하트 마크, 별 마크, and 재활용 마크. For a company's symbol, 로고 is also common. In soccer there is also 마크하다, for marking an opposing player.

en: to be discovered; to be found

examples.en: An old letter was found in the drawer.

examples.ko: 공원에서 길을 잃은 강아지가 발견돼서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I'm glad the lost puppy was found in the park.

examples.ko: 집 근처에서 실종된 아이가 무사히 발견되었어요.
examples.en: The missing child was found safely near home.

examples.ko: 이 병은 일찍 발견되면 치료가 쉬워요.
examples.en: If this illness is detected early, treatment is easy.
I saw news that a new star had been discovered.
No trace of the culprit has been found yet.

explain: 내가 찾아내면 '발견하다', 찾아지는 쪽을 주어로 하면 '발견되다'예요. '찾다'는 일부러 찾는 느낌이고, '발견하다'는 우연히 눈에 띄는 경우에도 써요. 처음 만들어 내는 '발명'과는 달리 이미 있던 것을 알게 되는 거예요.

phrases.en: I found a wallet on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아내는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person who finds it is the subject.

phrases.en: The lost key hasn't been found yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 찾지 못했다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it has not been found yet.

phrases.en: The place where the cat was found is the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발견되다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 장소나 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attaches '발견되다' before a noun to talk about a place or time.
phrases.en_equiv: the place where it was found

explain_en: When you find something, it is '발견하다'; when the thing found is the subject, it is '발견되다'. '찾다' feels like searching on purpose, while '발견하다' also fits something that catches your eye by chance. Unlike '발명' (inventing), it means coming to know something that was already there.
